title: The Bird Parliament
author: attar
attributionNote: The attribution is not disputed in the scholarship this catalogue follows.
description: The birds of the world gather to choose a king and set out under the hoopoe, Tajidar, to find the Simurgh beyond the mountain of Qaf. Each bird confesses the fault that holds it back, and the thirty who survive the journey discover that the Simurgh they sought is themselves. FitzGerald's abridged rendering keeps the frame and many of the tales in a verse that is closer to his Omar Khayyam than to a literal Persian edition.
historicalContext: Attar's Conference of the Birds was composed in Nishapur in the twelfth century. FitzGerald worked on this abridgement in 1857; it was published posthumously in the Letters and Literary Remains of Edward FitzGerald (1889). The text used here is the proofed public-domain transcription made for sacred-texts.com in 2007.
availabilityNote: Streamed from the Internet Archive at read time: the proofed plain-text derivative of the scan is fetched and split at the chapter headings it prints. The 1889 translation by Edward FitzGerald is public domain in the United States.
